title: Detect the Most Active Transaction Window
real_world_story: A fraud monitoring system receives transaction amounts in chronological order. A sudden increase in transaction activity within a short period may require additional investigation.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Transaction amounts recorded in chronological order
real_world_connection.target_represents: A fixed monitoring period containing K consecutive transactions
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Sliding Window for efficiently calculating the highest transaction total within any consecutive monitoring period

problem_statement: Given an array of transaction amounts and an integer K, find the maximum total transaction amount among all contiguous windows containing exactly K transactions.
task: Identify the K consecutive transactions with the highest total amount.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated transaction amounts. The third line contains K.
output_format: Print the maximum sum of any contiguous group of exactly K transaction amounts.

examples.explanation: The window 150, 400, 300 has the highest total of 850.
The window 200, 150 has the highest total of 350.

expected_algorithm.name: Sliding Window
expected_algorithm.reason: A sliding window updates the transaction total by removing the outgoing transaction and adding the incoming transaction instead of recalculating every window.

hint: Calculate the sum of the first K transactions.
Move the window one transaction at a time.
Subtract the transaction leaving the window.
Add the transaction entering the window.
Keep track of the maximum window sum.
real_world_takeaway: Sliding Window techniques allow monitoring systems to detect unusually high transaction activity over fixed time periods efficiently.
